record.file_problem: Repo metadata and README/file list only; code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports results from weight edits that use refusal directions and measure refusal delivery, but does not reproduce the original direct projection ablation method.
record.gate_note: The README reports refusal/delivery and benign KL results for Apostate's diode and KCRN edits. Setup instructions, method settings, benchmark options, and cited comparisons without reported outcomes are not result rows. No addition-to-induce-refusal result is reported; benign KL is not a general-capability benchmark.
record.test_reason: The repo builds weight edits from the difference-in-means refusal direction and reports refusal/delivery on held-out JailbreakBench prompts, plus benign KL, across several released instruct models. These are results on whether a direction-based weight edit removes refusal (V2) and whether subtracting that direction removes refusal (V1). The method differs from the original: a conditional gated-neuron subtraction (diode) or a closed-form writer nulling (KCRN), not full projection at every layer and position. Evidence is README-only and has not been peer reviewed.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors also claim that conditional (gated) removal of the refusal direction beats unconditional whole-direction abliteration on the delivery-versus-KL frontier. They say Granite and Gemma hold refusal harder and need per-model settings. They claim very low KL means capability is intact, which no reported benchmark verifies.
record.recipe_differences: The repo describes conditional diode subtraction using a gated MLP neuron and unconditional KCRN nulling of writers; neither is the original direct residual-direction projection procedure. Tool repo; code was not read or run.
record.method_sensitivity: The README says diode strength and gate-rate settings trade delivery against KL by model, and that Gemma and Granite use different settings from Qwen.
record.problems: Evidence is README-reported only and the code was not read or run. No uncertainty estimates are given. Benign KL is the reported preservation measure and does not directly establish general capability retention. The Qwen2.5-7B description lacks evaluation details.
record.rows_left_out: No additional reported refusal/delivery or KL outcome was left out. The README discusses benchmark suites and cited comparisons but gives no further measured results for them.

untested.parts: Inducing refusal by adding the direction. Unconditional full-layer and full-position projection ablation. General capability benchmarks: the README lists humaneval, mbpp and gsm8k suites but reports no results, and benign KL is only a proxy.
Capability retention on standard benchmarks. No baseline refusal rates are reported for Gemma 4, Granite 4 or Qwen3.8-27B. No uncertainty is reported.
Not tested. KCRN's harmful rank of 16 suggests multi-dimensional keys, but this is not evaluated as a claim.
Not tested; directions are fit separately for each model.
Qwen3 is a reasoning model, but no reasoning-specific analysis is reported.

missing.what: Figures that may contain further results: a before/after refusal plot, a refusal-vs-KL frontier, and a comparison against Heretic.
A claim that whole-direction removal typically costs 0.1+ KL. No measured comparison is given in the text.

record.verdict_notes: This is a tool README with no uncertainty estimates, and the code was not run. Delivery is judged by the HarmBench classifier on JailbreakBench held-out prompts (n=96). Most cross-architecture rows lack an unedited baseline. The text contains no instructions aimed at the reader.

versions.untested_parts: The reported edits are conditional diode or KCRN weight edits, not projection of one residual direction out of every layer and position. No addition experiment is reported, and benign KL does not establish that other abilities are largely intact.
The README reports the tool's weight-edit results, but does not report a release-specific result for each published checkpoint. The Qwen2.5-7B description does not specify its evaluation protocol.
No jailbreak suppression mechanism or training against ablation is tested.
No comparison of a single direction against an affine, cone, or multi-direction account is reported.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision is reported.
Results cover multiple architectures, but the method is fit separately per model; the README does not test whether the same direction transfers across models, languages, or training stages.
No comparison of refusal-training procedures or training stages is reported.
No reasoning-model-specific test of the refusal-direction claim is reported.

statements.correction: Qwen3-8B (dense, fp16): refusal ~99% to 9.4%, delivery ~1% to 90.6%, held-out KL 0.00065, n=96 JBB held-out. Qwen3.8-27B (hybrid linear-attention VLM, NF4 fit, fp16 bake): delivery 71.9%, KL 0.00237, no baseline stated. Per-model strength and gate-rate settings differ.
statements.problem: Both numbers for this study are in the text, but they are different measures: ~99% to 9.4% is a refusal rate (r5) and 71.9% is a delivery rate (r8). The scale comparison is also confounded: the 27B is a hybrid linear-attention VLM fit in NF4, not a dense same-family scale-up of Qwen3-8B, and no unedited 27B baseline is reported.
